title: errors.AsType
short_description: errors.As with the target variable removed, so it fits inside an if.
summary: `errors.As` needs somewhere to put the result, so it takes a pointer to a variable you have to declare on the line above. That variable then lingers in scope, and passing the wrong thing is a run-time panic rather than a compile error. `errors.AsType[T]` returns the value and a bool, which turns three lines into one and moves the mistake to compile time.
diagram_caption: Both walk the same Unwrap chain. The difference is where the answer goes: into a variable you declared, or back as a return value.
